newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare gains at close on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare gains at close on profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking pared gains at the Mexican bolsa close Wednesday, after stocks had risen in a technical correction over most of the day, traders said.
"We pulled back one-third of losses made after four straight falls, and some trading desks with very short positions took profits," said a trader at the Bancomer brokerage.
The blue-chip IPC index closed up 19.19 points, or 0.59 percent, at 3,273.16. Volume was brisk at 116.9 million shares traded, although this figure was inflated by cross-trades.
Analysts also put gains and increased volume down to a partial return of foreign investors.

"I feel you could say the bolsa is trying to get its year-end rally going, after almost four months in the doldrums. Foreigners have shaken off some of the lethargy now and it's not much of a sellers' market," said Alexander Anderson, research director at the Abaco brokerage.
On the broad market, 112 stocks were traded, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 56 to 32.
Financial stock Banacci headed the leaders list after its debt rating was raised, traders said.

Situr, the tourism arm of the debt-ridden Sidek group, led decliners in the wake of news that it had requested an extension to a standstill agreement. Under the agreement, creditors suspend efforts to collect for another period of time.
Shipping company TMM followed Situr on the down side. Traders said the share was still reeling from a subsidiary's hefty bid for a privatized rail concession.
